To close: parametrise over release 13..20 × subtype 0..31, field id 0..255 and revoke cause 0..255, with literal expected first-release tables, asserting encode succeeds exactly for the defined ones and raises ReleaseRefused otherwise.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |
| VP1-REL-004 | Subtype 14 is read per release | **PARTIAL** | test_release.py test_subtype_14_means_different_messages_either_side_of_rel_18 | 'From identical bytes' is not exercised: the codec check builds a FloorMessage object and calls name_of, with no decode of one wire buffer. It asserts only that Rel-17 != Rel-18, so swapped names would pass. Rel-20 is not checked. The exact names are asserted only on the subtype_name table, not on what the codec reports. To close: encode one subtype-14 packet, decode the same bytes with Codec(Rel-17..20), and assert the reported name equals 'Floor Queued Cancel' at 17 and 'Queued Floor Requests' at 18, 19 and 20.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |
| VP1-REL-005 | Wrong release is not malformed | **PARTIAL** | test_release.py test_a_rel_17_deployment_refuses_a_rel_19_message_on_the_wire<br>test_release.py test_wrong_release_is_distinguishable_from_malformed | The ReleaseRefused clause is met. The two counter clauses are asserted nowhere: floor_wrong_release (service/media.py:250) and floor_malformed (service/media.py:255) exist, but no test checks that a Rel-19 message received by a Rel-17 media session increments the first and not the second. A class-hierarchy check is not a counter check. To close: send a Rel-19 Floor Revoke Request to a Rel-17 service/media floor socket and assert counters floor_wrong_release == 1 and floor_malformed == 0.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |
| VP1-REL-006 | Release is in the audit record | **PARTIAL** | test_network.py test_every_audit_record_names_the_network | 'Every audit record' is covered by one record, hand-emitted via rt.auditor.emit(SESSION_REFUSED). No record produced by real session flow (hook-invocation, session-admitted, session-established, session-failed, released) or read back from the durable store is checked. The expected value is built from profile.identifier() itself, so the test would still pass if identifier() dropped the hash. To close: run a call through SipCore, then for every record in rt.store.audit_records(cid), assert the identity matches a literal pattern name/version/<16-hex hash>+Rel-NN+net-name/version/hash with the configured release.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |
| VP1-REL-007 | Signalling warning codes are release-gated | **PARTIAL** | test_release.py test_a_release_bound_code_is_gated_but_a_rel_13_code_is_not<br>test_release.py test_a_release_without_the_code_still_explains_the_refusal<br>test_release.py test_warning_code_179_does_not_exist_before_rel_17 | Only code 179 is shown degrading, and only at Rel-16. Rel-13–15 are not tested for 179. The other release-bound codes the platform emits are not tested for degradation at all: 185, 186 and 187 (Rel-18, ADHOC_WARNING_TEXTS) at Rel ≤17, where frmcs ad hoc is configurable per test_adhoc.py. 'Does not raise' is shown only for that one path. To close: parametrise over every (reason_code, emitted code) in WARNING_TEXTS and ADHOC_WARNING_TEXTS × release 13..20, asserting that where the code post-dates the release the Warning carries the phrase without the number, the status equals the in-release status and is 4xx/5xx, and no exception is raised.; reviewed 2026-09-28 by independent review (agent) |
